stem: When teaching sexual health after transplantation, which infection-prevention measure aligns with standard references?

options.text: Encourage use of condoms to prevent sexually transmitted diseases
Condoms are unnecessary because immunosuppression prevents sexually transmitted diseases
Sexually transmitted disease prevention requires permanent abstinence for all recipients
Only pediatric recipients need sexually transmitted disease prevention counseling

explanation.rationale_correct: Sexual health teaching includes encouraging use of condoms to prevent sexually transmitted diseases along with contraception and pregnancy counseling.

rationale_incorrect.B: Immunosuppressed recipients remain at infection risk and benefit from condom counseling.
rationale_incorrect.C: Condom use is recommended rather than universal permanent abstinence.
rationale_incorrect.D: Sexual health teaching applies to adult recipients as well as pediatric counseling on related topics.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → k. Sexual health → iii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Encourage use of condoms to prevent sexually transmitted diseases

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → k. Sexual health → iii. (condoms to prevent sexually transmitted diseases); PDF p. 121 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Condom/STD-prevention angle distinct from pregnancy-timing counseling (cctc-1091) and pediatric HPV teaching (cctc-1087); anchor verified on Cupples p. 121.

stem: A female transplant recipient asks about oral contraception after transplantation. Which counseling point aligns with standard references?

options.text: Discuss oral contraception with the provider because it may be contraindicated due to thromboembolic risk
All oral contraceptives are safe without provider discussion in every recipient
Oral contraception is the only recommended contraceptive method after transplant
Thromboembolic risk is irrelevant to contraception counseling after transplantation

explanation.rationale_correct: Sexual health teaching includes discussing oral contraception with the provider because it may be contraindicated due to risk of thromboembolic events.

rationale_incorrect.B: Oral contraception requires individualized provider discussion rather than universal safety.
rationale_incorrect.C: Multiple contraceptive and pregnancy-planning options are discussed rather than oral contraception alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Thromboembolic risk is specifically cited as a reason for provider discussion.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → k. Sexual health → iv.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Discuss use of oral contraception with provider; may be contraindicated due to risk of thromboembolic events

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → k. Sexual health → iv. (oral contraception may be contraindicated due to thromboembolic risk); PDF p. 121 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Oral-contraception counseling angle distinct from condom teaching (cctc-1122) and pregnancy postponement (cctc-1091); anchor verified on Cupples p. 121.

stem: When teaching recipients about appearance changes after transplantation, which effect aligns with standard long-term medication references?

options.text: Weight gain and hair loss may occur with certain medications
Immunosuppression prevents all cosmetic or body-image changes
Hair loss never occurs after transplantation
Weight gain is impossible on any immunosuppressive regimen

explanation.rationale_correct: Appearance teaching notes that transplantation may lead to body image changes associated with medications and surgical sequelae, including weight gain and hair loss with certain drugs.

rationale_incorrect.B: Medication and surgical sequelae can affect appearance and body image.
rationale_incorrect.C: Hair loss may occur with certain immunosuppressive medications.
rationale_incorrect.D: Weight gain may occur with certain medications rather than being impossible.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Weight gain and hair loss may occur with certain medications

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → m. Appearance → ii. (weight gain and hair loss with certain medications); PDF p. 121 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Body-image/appearance angle distinct from cyclosporine cosmetic effects (cctc-3045) and sexual-health counseling (cctc-1122); anchor verified on Cupples p. 121.

stem: A coordinator is updating sexual and reproductive health teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Recipients should discuss potential pregnancy with the transplant team and obstetrician.
Males may father a child after transplantation.
Pregnancy should begin immediately at hospital discharge without team discussion.
Pregnancy is generally postponed until 1 year after transplant when immunosuppressant doses are likely lower.

explanation.rationale_correct: Pregnancy planning includes team and obstetric discussion, males may father children after transplant, and pregnancy is generally postponed until 1 year post-transplant. Statement III is false because immediate discharge pregnancy without discussion is not recommended.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also true—pregnancy is generally postponed until 1 year post-transplant.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement III is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false because pregnancy requires coordinated planning rather than immediate discharge initiation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → l. Pregnancy after transplantation
primary_anchor.quote_hint: discuss potential pregnancy with transplant team and obstetrician … Males may father a child … Postpone pregnancy until 1 year after transplant

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → l. Pregnancy after transplantation → i.–iii. (team/obstetric discussion, males may father child, postpone until 1 year); PDF p. 121 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Reproductive-health combo distinct from pregnancy-timing recall (cctc-1091) and condom teaching (cctc-1122); anchor verified on Cupples p. 121.
